product.title: The AI That Can't Burn Your Business: Build a Safe AI Operator
product.note: Repointed 2026-10-01 from the Shopify listing to ATLAS Academy (shop.mapfront.io), the store every bio now links to. The price is read from the store's public catalog.json.

lessons.title: The week-one failure
lessons.hook: I gave my AI agent my bank login on day one. Here's why you shouldn't.
lessons.line: Most agent projects fail because the agent gets hands before it has eyes.

lessons.title: Collectors only read
lessons.hook: My AI watched my business for two weeks before it was allowed to touch anything.
lessons.line: Your first collector only reads: is the website up, how full is the inbox, what sold today.

lessons.title: Unknown is not OK
lessons.hook: The worst bug an AI agent can have is saying everything's fine.
lessons.line: A check that can't run says unknown, grey and dashed, never green.

lessons.title: Fresh reads
lessons.hook: Ask your AI how much you made today. Mine refuses to guess.
lessons.line: Every figure is read now, from the source, with the time it was read.

lessons.title: The model picks names, not code
lessons.hook: My AI can't run code. That's why I trust it.
lessons.line: The model chooses from a list of actions. It can't write a shell command or a query.

lessons.title: Things that are never allowed
lessons.hook: There are five things my AI will never do, even if I beg it.
lessons.line: Moving money, changing DNS, deleting, revoking keys and rewriting its own code are never allowed.

lessons.title: Silence is never consent
lessons.hook: My AI asked me something and I ignored it. Here's what it did: nothing.
lessons.line: Unanswered requests expire. They never run on a timeout.

lessons.title: Prompt injection in the wild
lessons.hook: This email tried to take over my AI. It failed.
lessons.line: Emails, web pages and comments can try to give your agent orders. Mine treats them as data.

lessons.title: Guard the machine your agent lives on
lessons.hook: Who watches my AI? Another AI that can't act.
lessons.line: A second watcher keeps an eye on the network the agent runs on, and it can only report.

lessons.title: Clipping, made easier
lessons.hook: I stopped clipping streams by hand. My agent cuts the moment, captions it and queues it.
lessons.line: A clipping campaign has rules; the agent reads them first, cuts to them, and never posts what it can't verify.

lessons.title: AI consultant, not AI agency
lessons.hook: Don't sell an AI agency. Build one operator a client can watch, and show the receipts.
lessons.line: A consultant hands over one system with eyes before hands; an agency promises hands it can't control.

lessons.title: How to use Claude correctly
lessons.hook: Claude isn't a chatbot. It's a worker that needs a closed menu of actions.
lessons.line: Give it the names of what it may do, validate every argument, and let it answer unknown.

lessons.title: AI automation, made easier
lessons.hook: Four systems run my business while I sleep: a watcher, a picker, a gate and a log.
lessons.line: Watch first, pick from a closed list, ask before acting, write everything down.

lessons.title: Converting your website, made easier
lessons.hook: Your website doesn't need a chatbot. It needs an agent that asks before it answers a customer.
lessons.line: It drafts the reply, shows you the dry run, and nothing leaves until you tap yes.

lessons.title: YouTube Shorts, made easier
lessons.hook: I don't upload Shorts by hand. An agent queues them, and it can't post what failed a check.
lessons.line: Every post goes through one door, with a gate before it and a record after it.

lessons.title: An AI course, made easier
lessons.hook: Most AI courses teach prompts. This one teaches what your agent must never be able to do.
lessons.line: Twenty-eight lessons, an exercise in each, and a starter agent with its tests passing.

lessons.title: The ground rules
lessons.hook: Eight rules I follow before I let AI sell anything for me.
lessons.line: Never guess a number, permission in writing, drafts before sends, and money out is always your own click.

lessons.title: Permission first, and where to find it
lessons.hook: Clipping a streamer without a campaign is how a channel gets deleted.
lessons.line: No campaign, no clip: cut only footage the owner has put up for clippers, with the rules page saved.

lessons.title: Reading a campaign's rules
lessons.hook: Most rejected clips are good clips that broke a rule nobody read.
lessons.line: Fill in one card per campaign: source, platforms, length, required tags, draft step, how to claim.

lessons.title: Finding the moments
lessons.hook: I don't watch three hours of stream. I read a transcript and judge a short list.
lessons.line: A model proposes moments with exact first and last lines; you keep the ones that start clean and end.

lessons.title: Cutting, captions and formats
lessons.hook: If your clip doesn't make sense with the sound off, it doesn't work.
lessons.line: Vertical, short caption lines inside the safe area, one layout per campaign, checked before it leaves.

lessons.title: One product, from what you already know
lessons.hook: Sell the thing you've actually done, to the person you were before you'd done it.
lessons.line: Pick one small product from what people already ask you for, and name its buyer in one sentence.

lessons.title: Building it, with the model as editor
lessons.hook: Don't ask AI to write your product. Make it interview you instead.
lessons.line: You supply the steps and mistakes; the model shapes them, and you test the result as a stranger.

lessons.title: The honest product page
lessons.hook: A new product has no reviews. A page that says so outsells one that fakes them.
lessons.line: Describe what's inside with counted numbers, say who it isn't for, and leave out urgency and invented praise.

lessons.title: Getting paid and delivering
lessons.hook: Landing on a thank-you page proves nothing. Ask the payment provider every time.
lessons.line: A payment link takes the money; delivery checks the payment is real and not refunded before giving files.

lessons.title: What dropshipping really is
lessons.hook: When you dropship, you are the seller. Not the supplier. You.
lessons.line: Returns, delivery promises and product safety are yours, so start with one product you understand.

lessons.title: Order the sample
lessons.hook: Before I sell anything, I buy it myself and time the delivery.
lessons.line: Order like a customer, keep a diary, measure it, photograph it, and put the real delivery time on the page.

lessons.title: What no automation may do
lessons.hook: Five things my AI can never do, even if a message tells it to.
lessons.line: Money out, domain and account settings, deleting, keys, and its own rules stay with you, enforced by setup.

lessons.title: Why chatbots can be confidently wrong
lessons.hook: A chatbot sounding sure is not the same as a chatbot being right.
lessons.line: Sort any AI answer into an idea, a claim to check, or an action that needs your approval.

lessons.title: The CLEAR prompt
lessons.hook: "Write an email" is why your AI answers are useless.
lessons.line: Turn a vague request into a clear prompt that gets a useful answer the first time.

lessons.title: Check before you trust
lessons.hook: Before you repeat what an AI told you, check three things.
lessons.line: Check dates, sources and numbers against the original, and keep a simple fact-check log.

lessons.title: Remove private details before you paste
lessons.hook: Stop pasting your whole life into a chatbot.
lessons.line: Strip names, ID numbers, health and money details and passwords out first, and still get a useful answer.

lessons.title: Privacy, memory, and incognito
lessons.hook: Three settings in your Claude account you should look at today.
lessons.line: Whether chats help train models, what it remembers about you, and how to have a chat that isn't saved.

lessons.title: Explain this letter
lessons.hook: That confusing letter from your landlord? Have AI explain it, then check it.
lessons.line: Give Claude a document and get a plain-English summary plus a list of what to double-check.

lessons.title: Build your first Skill
lessons.hook: You can teach Claude a task once and reuse it forever.
lessons.line: Write a Skill file, upload it, and test it on made-up task lists.

lessons.title: What never goes into an AI
lessons.hook: Some things never go into an AI. Here's how to sort them.
lessons.line: Sort information into never, with care, or fine, whether you type it, upload it or say it.

lessons.title: Voice-clone and family emergency scams
lessons.hook: If a family member calls in a panic asking for money, hang up and call back.
lessons.line: Call back on a number you already know, and agree a family safe word as a second check.

lessons.title: What a workflow is
lessons.hook: Every repeated chore is a trigger, some steps and a result.
lessons.line: Break a chore into those three parts and draw it as a workflow on paper.

lessons.title: Create your Claude account
lessons.hook: Claude never asks you to create a password. If something does, stop.
lessons.line: Set up your own account on your own phone and ask it one test question.

lessons.title: Remove private details before you paste
lessons.hook: Before you show AI a message, cover the private parts.
lessons.line: Take out names, numbers, health and money details and passwords first.

lessons.title: Voice mode and the mobile app
lessons.hook: You don't have to type. You can just talk to it.
lessons.line: Talk to Claude out loud and hear it answer, using voice mode on your phone.

lessons.title: Explain this letter
lessons.hook: A confusing letter in the post? Take a photo, with the numbers covered.
lessons.line: Get a plain-English summary of a letter, then check it against the original.

lessons.title: What never goes into an AI
lessons.hook: Three piles: never, with care, and fine.
lessons.line: Sort information into three piles before any of it goes into an AI.

lessons.title: Voice-clone and family emergency scams
lessons.hook: A voice on the phone can be copied. Pick a family safe word.
lessons.line: Choose a safe word, and practise hanging up and calling back.

lessons.title: Deepfakes, seeing is not believing
lessons.hook: A surprising video is not proof. Check a second source.
lessons.line: Check a surprising picture or video using a second, separate source.

lessons.title: Phishing and AI-polished messages
lessons.hook: Hurry, secrecy and strange payment requests: three warning signs.
lessons.line: Spot three warning signs in a text or an email before you answer it.
